phrases.text: Question 3 is about who may vote in Virginia.
Today, a felony conviction takes away the right to vote for life, unless the Governor restores it.
The amendment would make voting a fundamental right of every qualified Virginian.
A person convicted of a felony would lose the vote while incarcerated, regaining it on release without applying to the Governor.
Incapacity would cost the vote only if a court finds the person does not understand the act of voting.
The Department of Planning and Budget estimates $205,000 for public notice of statewide referendums, not the amendment itself.
Virginia's explanation includes no official argument for the amendment.
Virginia's explanation includes no official argument against the amendment.
A yes vote restores the vote on release.
A no vote leaves restoration to the Governor.
